notes.claim: Standard form is a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of ten, also called scientific notation.
NIST recommends choosing prefixes so values lie between 0.1 and 1000, using only prefixes for powers of 10 that are multiples of 3.
Milli is the metric prefix for one thousandth, 10⁻³.

sources.title: What is standard index form in maths? - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: In standard form, numbers are recorded as a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of ten. This is also called standard index form or scientific notation

sources.title: NIST Guide to the SI, Chapter 7: Rules and Style Conventions for Expressing Values of Quantities | NIST
sources.quote: prefix symbols should be chosen in such a way that numerical values are between 0.1 and 1000, and that only prefix symbols that represent the number 10 raised to a power that is a multiple of 3 should be used.

sources.title: Milli- - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Milli (symbol m ) is a unit prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one thousandth (10 −3 ).
